**Synopsis:**
Under a sweeping Trump-brokered U.S.-Venezuela oil deal, U.S.-backed NABEP (controlled by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt) is awarded 14 new oilfield contracts in Venezuela, displacing Chinese operators (China Concord Resources, Sinopec, CNPC) and a Russian firm. The U.S. government secures a 35% equity stake, preferential access to 20% of production at cost, right of first refusal on the remaining 80%, and veto power over NABEP's board. Oil is being redirected from China to U.S. refineries in Texas and Louisiana. The deal is framed as both a geopolitical and economic realignment of Venezuela's vast oil reserves toward U.S. interests.
